C-SPEC-LINT-RULES-SPLIT.Summary: Split the 1766-line src/lib/spec-lint.ts rule monolith into a src/lib/spec-lint/ directory organized by artifact kind behind an API-preserving barrel, so each future rule change stops growing one file.
C-SPEC-LINT-RULES-SPLIT.Problem: spec-lint.ts is a pure, well-scoped linter but internally monolithic: only 6 exports are public while roughly 1500 lines of private rule functions for all artifact kinds (spec, plan, design-context), cross-file checks, delegated-extraction validation, and parsing sit in one file between parseSpecXml and lintSpecArtifacts. Every rule addition or adjustment edits the same file, and the file keeps growing.

Goals.Goal: src/lib/spec-lint/ with a re-export-only barrel index.ts preserving the complete current public API, a parser module, per-kind rule modules, a cross-file rule module, and a delegated-extraction module.
Behavior-preserving: identical findings, severities, rule ids, line numbers, cache keys, and extraction results for the same inputs.
M-SPEC-LINT remains the owning graph module with Paths updated to the new files and spec-lint-cache.ts untouched except for import resolution that already works through the barrel.

Constraints.Constraint: Pure structural move: no rule semantics, finding text, severity mapping, LINT_VERSION bump, or public API change; LINT_VERSION stays 2 so cached verdicts remain valid.

Split zones: parser.ts (xmlMode event-stream parse, positioned element tree, artifact-kind detection, archive-path check), spec-rules.ts (spec and design-context template/identity rules), plan-rules.ts (plan template, task/wave/checkpoint identity, execution-section, and review-checkpoint rules), cross-file-rules.ts (plan-subset-of-spec and cross-artifact reference integrity), delegated-extraction.ts (extractDelegatedPlanDefinition typed extraction), index.ts (public barrel).
The barrel is re-exports only, with no htmlparser2 import and no rule implementation.
src/lib/spec-lint.test.ts and src/lib/spec-lint-cache.test.ts stay at their current paths and content; all consumers importing ../lib/spec-lint.js or ./spec-lint.js keep resolving.
Shared private helpers live in exactly one module; no duplication across rule modules.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No new lint rules, no rule relaxations or tightenings, no cache format change.
No changes to spec-lint-cache.ts behavior, the spec-guard plugin, commands/lint.ts, or workflow-contract re-exports.
No new graph modules; M-SPEC-LINT keeps owning the linter, and no per-rule-module anchors are added.
No test additions or renames; the existing 900-line suite passing unmodified is the behavior-preservation evidence.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: AC-01: src/lib/spec-lint.ts no longer exists; src/lib/spec-lint/index.ts re-exports its complete public API and every consumer import keeps resolving and typechecking.
AC-02: Rule functions are distributed into the zone modules named in the constraints with truthful file-local contracts, maps, and change summaries linking M-SPEC-LINT; shared helpers exist once.
AC-03: bun test on src/lib/spec-lint.test.ts, src/lib/spec-lint-cache.test.ts, and src/plugins/spec-guard/index.test.ts passes unmodified; bun run check, build, and pack:check pass.
AC-04: M-SPEC-LINT Paths list the new files instead of src/lib/spec-lint.ts, Purpose/Depends/Verification stay truthful, and grace lint and grace status pass.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun run build && bun run pack:check
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Target assertions verify the zone files exist, the barrel re-exports the previous API with no htmlparser2 import, and the old file is gone. The unmodified linter suite plus the cache and spec-guard suites are the behavior-preservation evidence because they exercise every rule family, cache keying, and the consuming plugin through the barrel.

Assumptions.Assumption: The zone boundaries follow the rule families visible in the current file; a rule function may move to an adjacent zone during execution when its inputs reveal a clearer owner, recorded in the change summary, without adding or removing zones.

Approval provenance: the user explicitly instructed autonomous formalization of the five reviewed refactoring items; the review deferred this split to the next substantive rule change, and this bundle makes that split the formalized next change for the linter.
